clue.text: Spy desires to get into bus leaving university

indicators.note: to get into says the desires piece goes inside the shortened vehicle
leaving says the university letter departs from the vehicle word

parts.note: taken as the vehicle's own name
desires as a verb means urges

explanation.surface: A secret agent's longing to board a bus as he heads away from campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Spy is a real person here: Guy Burgess, one of the Cambridge spy ring, not a generic agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Burgess was one of the Cambridge Five, Soviet agents recruited at Cambridge University.

clue.text: Graduate given prize in northern town

parts.note: BA, a Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: A graduate awarded a prize in a town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacup is a small town in Lancashire, in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacup is a Lancashire town in the Rossendale valley of northern England.

clue.text: Odd European barrister

parts.note: rum is old-fashioned British slang for strange
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A strange European lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpole of the Bailey is a British TV and book series about an eccentric London barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace Rumpole is John Mortimer's fictional Old Bailey defence counsel.

clue.text: It's slippery, see — that's what we hear

definitions.note: a description of something, standing for the adjective meaning slippery

indicators.note: says the cathedral city is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a thing is slippery, and says it is by hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely, in Cambridgeshire, is one, and is pronounced EE-lee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something like an eel is wriggly and hard to grip, hence slippery.

clue.text: Feelings to hot up, sadly, on account of mistake in conversation

indicators.note: sadly says the preceding words come out badly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Emotions run high and someone blunders while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: An inadvertent verbal error, saying something one did not intend.

clue.text: Maiden ensnared by a more desperate stalker?

indicators.note: ensnared by says the maiden letter is caught inside the comparative word

parts.note: more dire, so more desperate
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman trapped by an increasingly frantic follower.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a stalker is only a sinister kind of fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker is an obsessive devotee, an extreme example of someone who adores another person.

clue.text: Hip pastor's hot on unconventional philosopher claiming spiritual insights

indicators.note: unconventional says the letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: A trendy clergyman is keen on an eccentric thinker with mystical claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Rudolf Steiner's spiritual science believe in knowledge of a spiritual world through inner perception.

clue.text: Plotter in country besieged by dull soldiers

indicators.note: besieged by says the country is surrounded by the dull word

parts.note: mat (matt) means without shine
China is a country
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A conspirator in a nation surrounded by uninspiring troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A schemer who devises crafty intrigues is a plotter.

clue.text: Artist and his creation, not one about to create delight

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician

indicators.note: not says the one and about letters are left out of the artist's work

parts.note: an artist creates a picture
I is the Roman numeral one
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A painter and his work, lacking the spark to create joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes I and C from PICTURE, leaving PTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is ecstatic joy, intense delight.

clue.text: Work of art upsetting maiden? There's something deceptive in it

indicators.note: in it says the deceptive piece is placed inside the upturned maiden word
in a down clue, upsetting says the maiden word is turned upside down

parts.note: a maiden over is a cricket over with no runs scored
a lie deceives

explanation.surface: An artwork that offends a young woman, with something false within it.
explanation.walkthrough: The maiden is cricket's over with no runs scored, not a young woman; 'upsetting' turns it upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievo is relief sculpture, with figures projecting from a flat background.

clue.text: Do without starter — entering, order ungarnished beef

indicators.note: entering says the order and ungarnished pieces go inside the shortened verb
without starter says the opening letter of the verb is dropped

parts.note: to do is to act
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
food with nothing added on top is plain

explanation.surface: A diner orders plain beef and skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a restaurant order, but beef is slang for a grievance, not the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech a beef is a grievance or grumble someone raises.

clue.text: Resin from underground deposit, soft inside

indicators.note: inside says the soft letter sits within the deposit word

parts.note: coal is mined from underground seams
P is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A resin sourced from a buried deposit with a soft core.
explanation.definitionFit: Copal is a hard tree resin used in making varnishes.

clue.text: A tiny bit goody-goody, one of the cricket sides

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for sanctimonious
the on side (leg side) is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A small piece of a sanctimonious person playing on one side of the cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket field is split into the off side and the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pion is a subatomic particle, about as tiny a bit of matter as there is.

clue.text: Run-time OU medic originally smashed, breaking record

definitions.text: Run-time OU medic originally smashed, breaking record

indicators.note: breaking says the scrambled letters split the record word open

parts.note: a file is a record kept on paper or computer

indicators.note: smashed says the run-time, OU and initial letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; also Oxford University

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of medic

explanation.surface: An Oxford University medical student shattered a record by running a timed distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes Roger Bannister, an Oxford medical student who in 1954 was the first to break this barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a mile in under four minutes was the famous athletic barrier Bannister broke first.

clue.text: Going round to protect John, upset and uncertain

indicators.note: to protect says the reversed toilet word is shielded inside the surrounding word

parts.note: ambient means surrounding, all around

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset says the toilet word is turned upside down

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, short form lav

explanation.surface: Circling to guard a man called John, troubled and hesitant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LAV into VAL. John is the lavatory, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Having mixed feelings and being unable to decide either way.

clue.text: The woman's small creature, mostly a retiring type

parts.note: the woman's is her

indicators.note: mostly says the small creature's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a mite is a tiny arachnid

explanation.surface: A woman owns most of a tiny creature that shies away.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse who withdraws from society is a classic retiring type.

clue.text: Material cased in lead, old stuff used in medical experiment

indicators.note: cased in says the material sits inside the lead symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
lace is a fabric

explanation.surface: Fabric sealed inside lead, old matter used in medical trials.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead is the metal, not a verb meaning to guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given to a control group in a drug trial is an inert substance used for comparison.

clue.text: Cold tops in container for ice or snow

indicators.note: in says the cold and tops pieces sit inside the container word

parts.note: an ice cream comes in a cone
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
A1 means first-rate, read as the letters AI

explanation.surface: A cold vessel holding ice or snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice or snow' looks like the definition, but ice belongs to the ice cream cone; only snow defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is long-standing slang for the powdered drug.

clue.text: Unwell girl's said we sound chirpy

indicators.note: said says the phrase is spoken, giving the insects' name

parts.note: sick Ada's: unwell is sick, and Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A poorly young woman's remark, voiced with a cheerful tone.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects make loud chirping calls, so they speak of themselves as chirpy.

clue.text: Financial unit not entirely innocent, I moan

indicators.note: not entirely says the letters come from part of the phrase, not all of it

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they are less than blameless over money.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimo is a hundredth of a currency such as the peseta or euro in Spain.

clue.text: Loutish son joins campaign

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to lobby is to campaign for a cause

explanation.surface: A boorish son signs up for a political push.
explanation.definitionFit: Slobby describes someone lazy and coarse, close in meaning to oafish or boorish.

clue.text: Trouble with fight breaking out? Rescue operation needed

indicators.note: breaking says the trouble word splits the fight word apart

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Trouble as a fight erupts; a rescue is called for.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial rescue of a failing company or bank, especially by government.

clue.text: Fruit worker gangster forced into car

indicators.note: forced into says the worker and gangster pieces are pushed inside the car word

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door car
an ant is the crossword's standard worker
Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A fruit-picker and a mobster are bundled into a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit worker' reads as one phrase, but fruit is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantaloupe is a variety of melon with orange flesh.

clue.text: See 12
What gets devoured when the foremost lady comes round?

definitions.text: What gets devoured when the foremost lady comes round?

indicators.note: comes round says the lady's letters surround the devoured word

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, the nation's leading lady
ate means devoured

explanation.surface: What gets eaten when the Queen visits?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the one doing the devouring is the Queen herself.
explanation.definitionFit: One who devours food at a royal visit is a diner.

clue.text: Good spirit to get old Irish leader half cut

indicators.note: half cut says only the first half of the leader's name is kept

parts.note: Eamon de Valera was Irish Taoiseach and President

explanation.surface: A spirited Irish politician gets half drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Half cut is British slang for drunk, hence the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist belief a deva is a benevolent divine being.

clue.text: Road runs into nightclub, maybe

indicators.note: into says the runs letter goes inside the club word

parts.note: a dive is a seedy nightclub or bar
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A road leading into a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a road, often a residential street or private approach.

clue.text: Good Scottish job with minimal English involvement? That points the way

parts.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good
E is the minimal form of English, its abbreviation
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A decent Scottish job with hardly any English presence.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost at a junction directs travellers along their route.

clue.text: Little person Sally sounding drunk

indicators.note: a drunk slurs the s into sh, so the sally word is said that way

parts.note: a sally is a sortie, a sudden attack

explanation.surface: Sally, a small woman, seems to be tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a name; it is the military sortie, slurred.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortie is informal for someone of small stature.

clue.text: Vehicle with rubbish, vehicle falling over

indicators.note: in this across clue, falling over says the rubbish-and-vehicle pair is read backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense
a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: A vehicle loaded with junk topples over.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm vehicle used for pulling ploughs and trailers.
